events.title: React open-sourced at JSConf US
events.summary: Facebook open-sourced React at JSConf US on May 29, 2013 — a declarative UI library with a virtual DOM.
events.about: React models UI as a function of state — components re-render when data changes, React diffs a virtual DOM and updates the real one efficiently. Powers Facebook, Instagram, Netflix frontends, Next.js, React Native mobile apps, and most modern SPAs. JSX mixes markup with JavaScript (controversial at launch, standard now).

narrative.whyChosen: React became the dominant frontend library and shifted the industry to component-based declarative UI.
narrative.whyImportant: The virtual DOM and one-way data flow influenced Vue, Svelte, and every major UI toolkit that followed.
narrative.problemSolved: Large Facebook UIs were hard to keep consistent; manual DOM sync did not scale with growing feature sets.

sources.title: Meta Engineering — React launched at JSConf (May 2013)

events.title: Android Studio announced
events.summary: Google announced Android Studio at Google I/O on May 15, 2013 — a dedicated Android IDE built on the IntelliJ Platform.
events.about: Android Studio replaced Eclipse ADT with Gradle builds, layout editors, emulators, and Kotlin-first tooling. It became the only officially supported Android IDE by 2015 — where millions of mobile developers write Java, Kotlin, and Jetpack Compose apps.

narrative.whyChosen: Android Studio consolidated Android development onto JetBrains' IDE platform under Google.
narrative.whyImportant: It ended the fragmented Eclipse plugin era for mobile Android teams.
narrative.problemSolved: Android developers juggled Eclipse plugins, Ant builds, and inconsistent emulator workflows.

sources.title: The Verge — Google announces Android Studio (May 15, 2013)
